## My Code (steps 4-6)

### Preparation

In the following two chunks of R code we load the necessary libraries and import the data.
```{r libraries}
#| message: false

# Load penguins
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r data}
#| cache: true
#| message: false

# Read data
penguins <- read.csv("data/data.csv")
```

### Results

In the following chunk we run the script that produces the plot.
```{r plot}
#| warning: false

# Plot penguins
ggplot(penguins, 
       aes(x = `Flipper.Length..mm.`, y = `Culmen.Length..mm.`)) +
        geom_point(aes(color = Species, shape = Species)) +
        scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange","purple","cyan4")) +
        labs(
                title = "Flipper and Culmen length",
                subtitle = "Dimensions for penguins at Palmer Station LTER",
                x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Culmen length (mm)",
                color = "Penguin species", shape = "Penguin species"
        ) +
        theme_minimal()
```

### Inline code

We can inline r code as well, like this simple adding of 25 + 25 = `{r} 25+25`.
And read from the imported data, for instance, there are `{r} sum(penguins$Species=='Gentoo penguin (Pygoscelis papua)')` Gentoo penguins and
`{r} sum(penguins$Species=='Chinstrap penguin (Pygoscelis antarctica)')` Chinstrap penguins in the dataset.
The most recently produced egg in the dataset was from `{r} max(penguins$Date.Egg, na.rm = T)`.

### Sourcing

```{r sourcing}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| file: "./scripts/do_addition.R"
```

We can add 10 and 20 using the external script's function. Its result is `{r} do_addition(10, 20)`.


## Meet the penguins (steps 1-3)

The `penguins` data from the [https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/](palmerpenguins package) contains size measurements for 344 penguins from three species observed on three islands in the Palmer Archipelago, Antarctica.

![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png)

Apparently, @horstPalmerArchipelagoPenguins2022 wrote something about penguins.
I also found an article about hypothermia in penguins [@handrichHypothermiaForagingKing1997], which I would never have thought of.
